questions.prompt: The volume profile gives 0.27 to the 15:00 hour. How many of a 12,000-share order does VWAP execution put in that hour?
options: 2,000 shares, one sixth of the order
questions.explanation: Each hour gets its fraction of the order: 12,000 × 0.27 = 3,240 shares. An equal split would give 12,000 / 6 = 2,000.

questions.prompt: 100 shares trade at $10.00 and 300 shares trade at $10.10. What is the VWAP?
options: $10.05, the average of the two prices
questions.explanation: Weight each price by its shares: (100 × 10.00 + 300 × 10.10) / 400 = 10.075 dollars. The plain average of $10.05 ignores that three times as many shares traded at $10.10.

questions.prompt: Why does an equal TWAP slice stand out more in the 12:00 hour than in the 10:00 hour?
options: The 12:00 hour trades half as many shares, so the same 2,000 shares are 1.82% of it instead of 0.91%
The bid-ask spread is always zero at 10:00
TWAP execution buys more shares at 12:00 than at 10:00
The volume profile is the same for every hour
questions.explanation: The market trades 110,000 shares at 12:00 and 220,000 at 10:00. A fixed 2,000 shares is twice as large a part of the quiet hour, so it is easier to notice and moves the price more.
